**Page 13 (p13:e105-p13:e109):**
- p13:e105: Notes about crown_test_mempool_preload_on_gpu_plus_bias.cu - wondering why time decreased even though matmul function wasn't using the preloaded data
- p13:e106: Realization - preload causes GPU warmup
- p13:e107: Explanation that mempool version includes GPU memory pool allocation time in measurement, while mempool_preload version loads weights before timing so that time is excluded
- p13:e108: Figure explaining the real reason for 50ms reduction - CUDA context initialization warmup effect. When pre_upload_weights_to_gpu calls cudaMalloc and cudaMemcpy before t_start, the CUDA driver wakes up for the first time, causing: 1. GPU context initialization (CUDA driver load), 2. GPU clock boosting (low power → max performance frequency), 3. JIT compilation (first kernel code compilation). These initialization costs all fall outside the timer interval. In contrast, mempool version has ensure_pool() → first cudaMalloc inside t_start, so all initialization costs are included in measurement.
- p13:e109: Conclusion - v1-1-2's 50ms reduction was due to GPU warmup, not preload

**Page 14 (p14:e110-p14:e120, p14:enh:e0-p14:enh:e11, p14:review:e0-p14:review:e11):**
- v1-1-3: crown_test_preload_fix - fixed to properly utilize preloaded W weights
- Changed double* type storing GPU addresses in neural network to Matrix* type
- pre_upload_weights_to_gpu changed from using memcpy2D to allocating and copying Matrix
- Compared with my_lirpa_mempool_preload_on_gpu.cu - no performance difference, so decided to run 100 times to check cumulative time
- Still no significant performance difference
- After ~500 runs, 5-10ms advantage
- Conclusion: preloading weights to reduce memcpy doesn't have much significance
- Rolled back to my_lirpa_mempool.cu (v1-1-1)
- v1-1-1-1: Introduced cuBlas to memory pool, changed matvec and matmul to use cuBlas instead of custom calculations //my_lirpa_mempool_cuBlas.cu

   - The 50ms reduction in v1-1-2 was due to GPU warmup from preload, not actual computation improvement
   - pre_upload_weights_to_gpu calling cudaMalloc/cudaMemcpy before t_start causes CUDA driver initialization (context init, clock boosting, JIT compilation) to fall outside timer
   - mempool version includes initialization costs inside timer because ensure_pool() → first cudaMalloc is inside t_start
